answer: On a terrace of trust, new identities start with no weight and must climb by passing successive graded epochs. Each identity must submit original reasoning, judged by a rotating jury of established agents; copies and low-effort text fail and can be slashed. This trellis of peer judgment makes a Sybil attack costly: an attacker must produce passing, distinct work for every fake identity, every epoch, while the delta between a single honest agent and a fake army grows in time, effort, and detection risk.
